questions.q_text: The dimensional formula of coefficient of viscosity is
questions.solution: From F = eta A (dv/dx), eta = F / (A dv/dx) gives ML^-1T^-1.

questions.q_text: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities has the same dimensional formula?
questions.solution: Both work and torque have dimensions ML^2T^-2, so the pair matches.

questions.q_text: A physical quantity P is given by P = a^2 b^3 / (c d). The percentage errors in a, b, c and d are 1 percent, 2 percent, 3 percent and 4 percent respectively. The maximum percentage error in P is
The dimensional formula of Planck's constant is
questions.solution: From E = h nu, h = E/nu = (ML^2T^-2)/(T^-1) = ML^2T^-1.

questions.q_text: The number of significant figures in the measurement 0.0060700 m is
questions.solution: Leading zeros are not significant; 6, 0, 7, 0, 0 are counted, giving 5 significant figures.

questions.q_text: The radius of a sphere is measured as 5.0 cm with a possible error of 0.1 cm. The maximum percentage error in the calculated volume of the sphere is
questions.solution: V is proportional to r^3, so dV/V = 3 (dr/r) = 3 x (0.1/5.0) x 100 = 6 percent.

questions.q_text: If force F, velocity v and time T are taken as fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula of mass is
questions.solution: Writing M = F^a v^b T^c and comparing powers gives a = 1, b = -1, c = 1, so M = F v^-1 T.

questions.q_text: The dimensional formula of the universal gravitational constant G is
questions.solution: From F = G m1 m2 / r^2, G = F r^2 / (m1 m2) = M^-1L^3T^-2.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a unit of energy?
questions.solution: Watt is the SI unit of power (J/s); erg, eV and kWh are all units of energy.

questions.q_text: Three masses are measured as 4.237 g, 2.51 g and 0.0067 g. Their sum, expressed to the correct number of decimal places, is
questions.solution: Sum = 6.7537 g; the least precise term (2.51 g) has 2 decimal places, so the result is 6.75 g.

questions.q_text: In a simple pendulum experiment g is calculated from g = 4 pi^2 L / T^2. If the error in measuring L is 1 percent and that in measuring T is 2 percent, the percentage error in g is
questions.solution: dg/g = dL/L + 2 dT/T = 1 + 2(2) = 5 percent.

questions.q_text: The dimensional formula of pressure gradient (rate of change of pressure with distance) is
questions.solution: Pressure has dimensions ML^-1T^-2; dividing by length L gives ML^-2T^-2.

questions.q_text: A car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s^2. The distance covered by it in the first 5 s is
A body moving with an initial velocity of 10 m/s is retarded uniformly at 2 m/s^2. Its velocity after 3 s is
A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the maximum height reached by it is
A car moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest with a uniform retardation of 5 m/s^2. The distance travelled before stopping is
questions.solution: Using v^2 = u^2 + 2as with v = 0, s = 400/(2 x 5) = 40 m.

questions.q_text: A particle starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 4 m/s^2. The distance covered by it during the 3rd second of its motion is
The area under an acceleration-time graph between two instants gives
questions.solution: Since a = dv/dt, the integral of a dt equals the change in velocity.

questions.q_text: The position of a particle is given by x = 2t^3 - 3t^2 + 4t, where x is in metre and t in second. The acceleration of the particle at t = 2 s is
A stone is dropped from the top of a tower 80 m high. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the speed with which it strikes the ground is
questions.solution: v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 80) = 40 m/s.

questions.q_text: Two trains move on parallel tracks in opposite directions with speeds 72 km/h and 54 km/h. The magnitude of the velocity of one train relative to the other is
questions.solution: Relative speed = 72 + 54 = 126 km/h = 126 x 5/18 = 35 m/s.

questions.q_text: A car covers the first half of a distance at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. Its average speed for the whole journey is
questions.solution: For equal distances, average speed = 2 v1 v2/(v1 + v2) = 2(40)(60)/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.q_text: A body starting from rest moves with constant acceleration. The ratio of the distances covered by it in the 1st, 2nd and 3rd seconds is
questions.solution: s_n is proportional to (2n - 1), which gives the ratio 1 : 3 : 5.

questions.q_text: A particle moving with uniform acceleration covers 40 m during the 4th second and 60 m during the 6th second of its motion. The total distance covered by it in the first 10 s is
A projectile is thrown with a speed of 20 m/s at 45 degrees to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, its horizontal range is
A body is projected with a speed of 20 m/s at 30 degrees to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the maximum height attained is
A ball is projected with a speed of 40 m/s at 30 degrees above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, its time of flight is
questions.solution: T = 2u sin(theta)/g = 2 x 40 x 0.5/10 = 4 s.

questions.q_text: A stone is thrown horizontally with a speed of 20 m/s from the top of a tower 45 m high. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the horizontal distance from the foot of the tower at which it lands is
questions.solution: t = sqrt(2h/g) = 3 s, so horizontal distance = 20 x 3 = 60 m.

questions.q_text: A particle moves in a circle of radius 5 m with a constant speed of 10 m/s. Its centripetal acceleration is
Two forces of 3 N and 4 N act at right angles to each other on a body. The magnitude of their resultant is
Two vectors, each of magnitude 10 units, have a resultant of magnitude 10 units. The angle between them is
questions.solution: R^2 = A^2 + B^2 + 2AB cos(theta) gives 100 = 200 + 200 cos(theta), so cos(theta) = -1/2 and theta = 120 degrees.

questions.q_text: A projectile fired at 15 degrees to the horizontal has a range R. For the same speed of projection, the same range is obtained at an angle of
questions.solution: Range is equal for theta and (90 - theta), so the complementary angle is 90 - 15 = 75 degrees.

questions.q_text: A body moves in a circle completing one revolution in 2 s. Its angular velocity is
questions.solution: omega = 2 pi/T = 2 pi/2 = pi rad/s (about 3.14 rad/s).

questions.q_text: A projectile is thrown with a speed of 20 m/s at 60 degrees to the horizontal. Its speed at the highest point of the trajectory is
questions.solution: At the top only the horizontal component survives: v = u cos(theta) = 20 x 0.5 = 10 m/s.

questions.q_text: A swimmer who can swim at 3 m/s in still water heads straight across a 300 m wide river flowing at 4 m/s. The distance he is carried downstream before reaching the opposite bank is
questions.solution: Crossing time = 300/3 = 100 s, so drift = 4 x 100 = 400 m.

questions.q_text: Two bodies are projected with the same speed at 30 degrees and 60 degrees to the horizontal. The ratio of their maximum heights is
questions.solution: H is proportional to sin^2(theta), so the ratio is sin^2(30)/sin^2(60) = 0.25/0.75 = 1 : 3.

questions.q_text: A constant force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 5 kg lying on a frictionless surface. The acceleration produced is
A ball of mass 2 kg strikes a wall normally with a speed of 5 m/s and rebounds with the same speed. The magnitude of the impulse imparted to the ball is
questions.solution: Impulse = change in momentum = m(v - u) = 2[5 - (-5)] = 20 N s.

questions.q_text: A block of mass 10 kg rests on a horizontal floor with coefficient of friction 0.2. A horizontal force of 30 N is applied to it. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the acceleration of the block is
questions.solution: Friction = mu m g = 0.2 x 10 x 10 = 20 N, so a = (30 - 20)/10 = 1 m/s^2.

questions.q_text: A block slides down a smooth inclined plane making an angle of 30 degrees with the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, its acceleration is
questions.solution: On a frictionless incline a = g sin(theta) = 10 x 0.5 = 5 m/s^2.

questions.q_text: Two masses of 6 kg and 4 kg hang from the two ends of a light inextensible string passing over a frictionless pulley. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the acceleration of the system is
The coefficient of static friction between a block and an inclined surface is 1/sqrt(3). The angle of repose is
questions.solution: tan(angle of repose) = mu = 1/sqrt(3), so the angle is 30 degrees.

questions.q_text: A man of mass 60 kg stands in a lift that accelerates upward at 2 m/s^2. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the normal reaction of the floor on him is
A block slides down a rough incline of angle 37 degrees (sin 37 = 0.6, cos 37 = 0.8) with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.5. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, its acceleration down the incline is
questions.solution: a = g(sin theta - mu cos theta) = 10(0.6 - 0.5 x 0.8) = 2 m/s^2.

questions.q_text: Two blocks of masses 2 kg and 3 kg are placed in contact on a frictionless horizontal surface. A horizontal force of 10 N is applied to the 2 kg block. The contact force between the blocks is
questions.solution: a = 10/5 = 2 m/s^2, so the force on the 3 kg block is 3 x 2 = 6 N.

questions.q_text: A passenger standing in a moving bus falls forward when the bus stops suddenly. This is because of
questions.opt_a: the inertia of rest of the passenger
questions.opt_b: the reaction force of the floor
questions.opt_c: the centripetal force acting on the passenger
questions.opt_d: the inertia of motion of the passenger
questions.solution: The lower body stops with the bus while the upper body continues to move due to inertia of motion.

questions.q_text: A car moving at 20 m/s is braked to rest on a road for which the coefficient of friction is 0.5. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the minimum stopping distance is
A gun of mass 2 kg fires a bullet of mass 20 g with a muzzle speed of 200 m/s. The recoil speed of the gun is
questions.solution: By conservation of momentum, V = m v/M = (0.02 x 200)/2 = 2 m/s.

questions.q_text: A force of 10 N displaces a body through 5 m, the force making an angle of 60 degrees with the displacement. The work done is
questions.solution: W = F s cos(theta) = 10 x 5 x 0.5 = 25 J.

questions.q_text: The kinetic energy of a body of mass 2 kg moving with a speed of 10 m/s is
A spring of force constant 200 N/m is compressed by 0.1 m. The potential energy stored in it is
A pump lifts 100 kg of water through a height of 10 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the power of the pump is
The speed of a 2 kg body increases from 5 m/s to 10 m/s. The work done on it is
questions.solution: By the work-energy theorem W = (1/2)m(v^2 - u^2) = 1 x (100 - 25) = 75 J.

questions.q_text: In a head-on elastic collision between two bodies of equal mass, one of which is initially at rest,
questions.opt_a: both move with half the initial speed
questions.opt_b: they stick together and move on
questions.opt_d: the moving body rebounds with the same speed
questions.solution: For equal masses in a one-dimensional elastic collision the velocities are simply interchanged.

questions.q_text: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 6 m/s collides with a stationary body of mass 4 kg and the two move together. The loss in kinetic energy is
questions.solution: Common velocity = 12/6 = 2 m/s; KE falls from 36 J to 12 J, so the loss is 24 J.

questions.q_text: A body of mass 1 kg falls freely from a height of 20 m. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, its kinetic energy just before striking the ground is
questions.solution: KE = mgh = 1 x 10 x 20 = 200 J.

questions.q_text: A ball dropped from a height of 10 m rebounds to a height of 2.5 m. The coefficient of restitution between the ball and the floor is
The work done by the centripetal force on a particle moving in a uniform circular motion over one full revolution is
questions.solution: The centripetal force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so W = F s cos(90) = 0.

questions.q_text: A car moves with a constant speed of 20 m/s against a total resistive force of 500 N. The power delivered by the engine is
A small body tied to a string is whirled in a vertical circle of radius 0.4 m. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the minimum speed it must have at the highest point to complete the circle is
questions.solution: At the top, minimum speed v = sqrt(gr) = sqrt(10 x 0.4) = 2 m/s.

questions.q_text: The moment of inertia of a uniform circular disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: Two particles of masses 2 kg and 3 kg are placed at x = 0 and x = 5 m respectively on the x-axis. The centre of mass of the system lies at
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: A force of 10 N is applied perpendicular to a spanner at a distance of 0.5 m from the axis of rotation. The torque produced is
questions.solution: Torque = r F sin(90) = 0.5 x 10 = 5 N m.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: A body of moment of inertia 2 kg m^2 rotates with an angular velocity of 5 rad/s. Its angular momentum is
questions.solution: L = I omega = 2 x 5 = 10 kg m^2/s.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: The moment of inertia of a thin ring of mass M and radius R about any of its diameters is
questions.solution: By the perpendicular axis theorem, 2 I_diameter = MR^2, so I_diameter = (1/2)MR^2.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: A uniform disc rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface. The fraction of its total kinetic energy that is rotational is
questions.solution: For a disc, rotational KE : translational KE = 1 : 2, so the rotational share of the total is 1/3.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: A ring rolls down without slipping on an incline of 30 degrees. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the acceleration of its centre of mass is
questions.solution: a = g sin(theta)/(1 + I/MR^2) = 10 x 0.5/2 = 2.5 m/s^2 for a ring.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: A flywheel of moment of inertia 4 kg m^2 rotates at an angular speed of 3 rad/s. Its rotational kinetic energy is
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: A torque of 20 N m acts on a body of moment of inertia 5 kg m^2. The angular acceleration produced is
questions.solution: alpha = torque/I = 20/5 = 4 rad/s^2.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: A dancer spinning at 2 rad/s with a moment of inertia of 6 kg m^2 pulls in her arms so that her moment of inertia becomes 2 kg m^2. Her new angular speed is
questions.solution: Angular momentum is conserved: omega2 = I1 omega1/I2 = (6 x 2)/2 = 6 rad/s.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: The moment of inertia of a uniform rod of mass 3 kg and length 1 m about an axis through one end and perpendicular to its length is
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: A solid sphere starts from rest and rolls without slipping down an incline, descending a vertical height of 7 m. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the speed of its centre at the bottom is
questions.solution: v = sqrt(10gh/7) = sqrt(10 x 10 x 7/7) = 10 m/s.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: The moment of inertia of a solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 0.2 m about a diameter is
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q_text: Taking the acceleration due to gravity at the earth's surface as 10 m/s^2, its value at a height equal to the radius of the earth above the surface is
questions.solution: g_h = g R^2/(R + h)^2 = g/4 = 2.5 m/s^2 when h = R.

questions.q_text: The escape speed from the surface of the earth, taking g = 10 m/s^2 and the earth's radius as 6400 km, is about
questions.solution: v_e = sqrt(2gR) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 6.4 x 10^6) = 1.13 x 10^4 m/s, about 11.3 km/s.

questions.q_text: Two point masses of 10 kg each are placed 1 m apart. Taking G = 6.67 x 10^-11 SI units, the gravitational force between them is
The orbital radius of a planet is 4 times that of another planet around the same star. The ratio of their periods of revolution is
questions.solution: By Kepler's third law T is proportional to r^(3/2), so the ratio is 4^(3/2) = 8.

questions.q_text: A satellite revolves in a circular orbit very close to the earth's surface. Taking g = 10 m/s^2 and R = 6400 km, its orbital speed is
questions.solution: v_o = sqrt(gR) = sqrt(10 x 6.4 x 10^6) = 8000 m/s = 8 km/s.

questions.q_text: The value of the acceleration due to gravity at a depth equal to half the radius of the earth, taking its surface value as 10 m/s^2, is
The period of revolution of a satellite orbiting just above the earth's surface, with g = 10 m/s^2 and R = 6400 km, is nearly
questions.solution: T = 2 pi sqrt(R/g) = 2 pi sqrt(6.4 x 10^6/10) = 5027 s, which is about 84 minutes.

questions.q_text: An astronaut inside an orbiting satellite feels weightless because
questions.opt_a: the astronaut and the satellite are both in free fall with the same acceleration
questions.opt_b: there is no gravitational force at that height
questions.opt_c: the astronaut is beyond the earth's gravitational field
questions.opt_d: the satellite moves with a very large constant speed
questions.solution: Both fall freely towards the earth with the same centripetal acceleration, so the normal reaction on the astronaut is zero.

questions.q_text: A planet has twice the mass of the earth and half its radius. If the escape speed from the earth is 11.2 km/s, that from the planet is
questions.solution: v_e = sqrt(2GM/R), so the new value is 11.2 x sqrt(2/0.5) = 11.2 x 2 = 22.4 km/s.

questions.q_text: Kepler's second law of planetary motion (the law of areas) is a direct consequence of the conservation of
questions.solution: The gravitational force is central, so the torque about the sun is zero and angular momentum is conserved.

questions.q_text: The time period of revolution of a geostationary satellite about the earth is
questions.solution: A geostationary satellite must match the earth's rotation, so its period is 24 hours in an equatorial orbit.

questions.q_text: A satellite of mass 200 kg revolves in a circular orbit at a height equal to the radius of the earth. Taking g = 10 m/s^2 and R = 6400 km, its binding energy is
questions.solution: Binding energy = GMm/(2r) = g R^2 m/(2 x 2R) = (10 x 6.4 x 10^6 x 200)/4 = 3.2 x 10^9 J.

questions.q_text: A steel wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 1 x 10^-6 m^2 is stretched by a force of 100 N. If Young's modulus of steel is 2 x 10^11 N/m^2, the elongation produced is
Young's modulus of a material has the same dimensional formula as
questions.solution: Y = stress/strain and strain is dimensionless, so Y has the dimensions of stress, i.e. pressure (ML^-1T^-2).

questions.q_text: The stress in a stretched wire is 2 x 10^8 N/m^2 and the corresponding strain is 1 x 10^-3. The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume of the wire is
questions.solution: u = (1/2) x stress x strain = 0.5 x 2e8 x 1e-3 = 1 x 10^5 J/m^3.

questions.q_text: The breaking stress of a metal is 4 x 10^8 N/m^2. The maximum load that a wire of this metal of cross-section 2 mm^2 can support is
questions.solution: F_max = breaking stress x area = 4e8 x 2e-6 = 800 N.

questions.q_text: A rod of Poisson's ratio 0.3 is stretched so that its longitudinal strain is 1 x 10^-3. The magnitude of the lateral strain produced is
questions.solution: Poisson's ratio = lateral strain/longitudinal strain, so lateral strain = 0.3 x 1e-3 = 3 x 10^-4.

questions.q_text: A wire is stretched by 1 mm by a force of 100 N applied gradually. The work done in stretching the wire is
Two wires of the same material carry equal loads. The second wire has twice the length and twice the radius of the first. The ratio of the elongation of the first wire to that of the second is
questions.solution: Delta L is proportional to L/r^2, so the ratio is (1/1) : (2/4) = 2 : 1.

questions.q_text: The bulk modulus of a liquid is 2 x 10^9 N/m^2. When the pressure on it is increased by 2 x 10^7 N/m^2, the fractional decrease in its volume is
questions.solution: Delta V/V = Delta P/B = 2e7/2e9 = 0.01, i.e. 1 %.

questions.q_text: The ratio of shearing stress to the corresponding shearing strain within the elastic limit is called
questions.solution: Shear stress divided by shear strain defines the modulus of rigidity (shear modulus).

questions.q_text: A wire of length 2 m and area of cross-section 1 x 10^-6 m^2 has Young's modulus 2 x 10^11 N/m^2. Treated as a spring, its force constant is
A wire of volume 2 x 10^-6 m^3 and Young's modulus 2 x 10^11 N/m^2 is stretched so that the strain in it is 1 x 10^-3. The elastic potential energy stored in the wire is
questions.solution: U = (1/2) Y (strain)^2 x volume = 0.5 x 2e11 x 1e-6 x 2e-6 = 0.2 J.

questions.q_text: A metal rod is clamped rigidly between two supports and heated through 10 degree C. If Y = 2 x 10^11 N/m^2 and the coefficient of linear expansion is 1.2 x 10^-5 per degree C, the thermal stress developed is
questions.solution: Thermal stress = Y x alpha x Delta T = 2e11 x 1.2e-5 x 10 = 2.4 x 10^7 N/m^2.

questions.q_text: The gauge pressure at a depth of 20 m below the free surface of a lake (density of water 1000 kg/m^3, g = 10 m/s^2) is
In a hydraulic lift the small piston has area 10 cm^2 and the large piston 100 cm^2. A force of 100 N applied on the small piston can lift a maximum load of
questions.solution: By Pascal's law F2 = F1 (A2/A1) = 100 x (100/10) = 1000 N.

questions.q_text: Water flows steadily through a pipe whose radius at one section is half that at another. The speed of flow in the narrower section compared with that in the wider section is
questions.solution: Continuity: Av = constant and A is proportional to r^2, so halving r makes v four times larger.

questions.q_text: Water of density 1000 kg/m^3 flows through a horizontal tube whose area falls from 10 cm^2 to 5 cm^2. If the speed in the wider part is 2 m/s, the pressure difference between the wider and the narrower parts is
questions.solution: Continuity gives v2 = 4 m/s; Bernoulli: Delta P = (1/2) rho (v2^2 - v1^2) = 0.5 x 1000 x 12 = 6000 Pa.

questions.q_text: A tank is filled with water to a height of 5 m. A small hole is made in its wall at the bottom. The speed of efflux of water from the hole is (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.solution: Torricelli's theorem: v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 5) = 10 m/s.

questions.q_text: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius 1 cm is (surface tension of the soap solution = 0.03 N/m)
questions.solution: A soap bubble has two surfaces: excess pressure = 4T/r = 4 x 0.03/0.01 = 12 Pa.

questions.q_text: The excess pressure inside a spherical liquid drop of radius 1 mm is (surface tension = 0.07 N/m)
questions.solution: A drop has a single surface: excess pressure = 2T/r = 2 x 0.07/1e-3 = 140 Pa.

questions.q_text: Water of surface tension 0.07 N/m rises in a capillary tube of radius 0.2 mm. If the angle of contact is zero and the density of water is 1000 kg/m^3, the height of the rise is (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.solution: h = 2T cos(theta)/(r rho g) = 2 x 0.07/(2e-4 x 1000 x 10) = 0.07 m = 7 cm.

questions.q_text: A spherical ball of radius 3 mm and density 3000 kg/m^3 falls through a liquid of density 1000 kg/m^3 and coefficient of viscosity 2 Pa s. Its terminal velocity is (g = 10 m/s^2)
A sphere of radius 1 mm moves with a speed of 0.05 m/s through a liquid of coefficient of viscosity 0.1 Pa s. The viscous drag acting on it is
questions.solution: Stokes' law: F = 6 pi eta r v = 6 pi x 0.1 x 1e-3 x 0.05 = 3 pi x 10^-5 N.

questions.q_text: The work done in increasing the radius of a soap bubble from 1 cm to 2 cm is (surface tension = 0.03 N/m)
A body weighs 50 N in air and 40 N when fully immersed in water. Its relative density is
questions.solution: Loss of weight = buoyant force = 10 N, so relative density = 50/10 = 5.

questions.q_text: The quantity of heat required to melt 10 g of ice at 0 degree C into water at 0 degree C is (latent heat of fusion = 80 cal/g)
questions.solution: Q = mL = 10 x 80 = 800 cal; temperature stays at 0 degree C during melting.

questions.q_text: 200 g of water at 90 degree C is mixed with 100 g of water at 30 degree C. The final temperature of the mixture is
questions.solution: Heat lost = heat gained: T = (200x90 + 100x30)/300 = 70 degree C.

questions.q_text: The heat needed to convert 10 g of ice at 0 degree C completely into steam at 100 degree C is (L_fusion = 80 cal/g, L_vaporisation = 540 cal/g, c_water = 1 cal/g/degree C)
The surface of a star behaves as a black body at 5800 K. Using Wien's constant 2.9 x 10^-3 m K, the wavelength at which it radiates maximum energy is
If the absolute temperature of a black body is doubled, the energy radiated per unit area per unit time becomes
questions.solution: Stefan's law: E is proportional to T^4, so doubling T gives 2^4 = 16 times.

questions.q_text: A black body of surface area 1 cm^2 is maintained at 1000 K. The power radiated by it is (sigma = 5.67 x 10^-8 SI units)
A body cools from 60 degree C to 50 degree C in 10 minutes in surroundings at 25 degree C. The time it takes to cool from 50 degree C to 40 degree C is
questions.solution: Newton's law: 10/10 = k(55-25) gives k = 1/30; then 10/t = (1/30)(45-25) so t = 15 min.

questions.q_text: A metal rod of length 1 m is heated through 50 degree C. If its coefficient of linear expansion is 2 x 10^-5 per degree C, the increase in its length is
questions.solution: Delta L = L alpha Delta T = 1 x 2e-5 x 50 = 1 x 10^-3 m = 1 mm.

questions.q_text: For an isotropic solid, the coefficients of linear, areal and volume expansion are related as
questions.solution: beta = 2 alpha and gamma = 3 alpha, so alpha : beta : gamma = 1 : 2 : 3.

questions.q_text: A metal rod of length 1 m and area of cross-section 1 x 10^-4 m^2 has thermal conductivity 200 W/m/K. If its ends are kept at a temperature difference of 100 K, the rate of heat flow through it in the steady state is
questions.solution: H = KA(Delta T)/L = 200 x 1e-4 x 100/1 = 2 W.

questions.q_text: Two rods of the same length and cross-section, having thermal conductivities K and 2K, are joined end to end. The free end of the first is at 0 degree C and that of the second at 90 degree C. The steady state temperature of the junction is
questions.solution: Equal heat current: K(T-0) = 2K(90-T) gives 3T = 180, so T = 60 degree C.

questions.q_text: The heat required to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water from 20 degree C to 70 degree C is (specific heat of water = 4200 J/kg/K)
questions.solution: Q = m c Delta T = 2 x 4200 x 50 = 4.2 x 10^5 J.

questions.q_text: 200 J of heat is supplied to a gas which does 50 J of work on its surroundings. The change in the internal energy of the gas is
questions.solution: First law: Delta U = Q - W = 200 - 50 = 150 J.

questions.q_text: One mole of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly at 300 K to twice its initial volume. The work done by the gas is (R = 8.314 J/K/mol, ln 2 = 0.693)
A monatomic ideal gas at 300 K is compressed adiabatically to one-eighth of its initial volume. Its final temperature is
questions.solution: T V^(gamma-1) = constant with gamma = 5/3: T2 = 300 x 8^(2/3) = 300 x 4 = 1200 K.

questions.q_text: A Carnot engine works between a source at 500 K and a sink at 300 K. Its efficiency is
A Carnot engine of efficiency 50 % rejects heat to a sink at 300 K. The temperature of its source is
A Carnot refrigerator works between 250 K and 300 K. Its coefficient of performance is
In a cyclic thermodynamic process, the net work done by the system in one complete cycle is equal to
questions.opt_a: The heat rejected to the sink
questions.opt_c: The net heat absorbed in the cycle
questions.solution: Over a cycle Delta U = 0, so by the first law Q_net = W_net.

questions.q_text: Two moles of a monatomic ideal gas are cooled adiabatically from 400 K to 300 K. The work done by the gas is (R = 8.314 J/K/mol)
For a rigid diatomic ideal gas, the molar heat capacity at constant pressure is (R = 8.314 J/K/mol)
questions.solution: Cv = 5R/2 and Cp = Cv + R = 7R/2 = 3.5 x 8.314 = 29.1 J/mol/K.

questions.q_text: A gas at a constant pressure of 2 x 10^5 Pa expands from a volume of 0.2 m^3 to 0.5 m^3. The work done by the gas is

An ideal gas is taken round a rectangular cycle on a P-V diagram between pressures 1 x 10^5 Pa and 3 x 10^5 Pa and volumes 1 x 10^-3 m^3 and 3 x 10^-3 m^3. The magnitude of the net work done per cycle is
questions.solution: Work per cycle = area enclosed = Delta P x Delta V = 2e5 x 2e-3 = 400 J.

questions.q_text: A heat engine of efficiency 25 % delivers 100 J of useful work per cycle. The heat rejected to the sink per cycle is
The root mean square speed of oxygen molecules (molar mass 32 g/mol) at 300 K is (R = 8.314 J/K/mol)
questions.solution: v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M) = sqrt(3 x 8.314 x 300/0.032) = 484 m/s approximately.

questions.q_text: For the molecules of an ideal gas at a given temperature, the ratio v_rms : v_average : v_most probable is nearly
questions.solution: The three speeds go as sqrt(3) : sqrt(8/pi) : sqrt(2) = 1.73 : 1.60 : 1.41.

questions.q_text: The rms speed of the molecules of a gas is 500 m/s at 300 K. At 1200 K the rms speed becomes
questions.solution: v_rms is proportional to sqrt(T); T becomes 4 times, so v_rms doubles to 1000 m/s.

questions.q_text: The average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule at 300 K is (k = 1.38 x 10^-23 J/K)
The internal energy of 2 moles of a monatomic ideal gas at 300 K is (R = 8.314 J/K/mol)
For a rigid diatomic ideal gas the number of degrees of freedom and the ratio Cp/Cv are respectively
questions.solution: A rigid diatomic molecule has f = 5, and gamma = 1 + 2/f = 1.4.

questions.q_text: For a non-linear triatomic ideal gas (translational and rotational degrees of freedom only), the ratio Cp/Cv is
questions.solution: f = 6 for a non-linear triatomic molecule, so gamma = 1 + 2/6 = 1.33.

questions.q_text: If the pressure of a gas is doubled while its temperature is kept constant, its mean free path
questions.solution: Mean free path is proportional to T/P, so doubling P at constant T halves the mean free path.

questions.q_text: One mole of helium is mixed with one mole of oxygen. The ratio Cp/Cv for the mixture is
questions.solution: Cv(mix) = (1x3R/2 + 1x5R/2)/2 = 2R and Cp(mix) = 3R, so gamma = 3R/2R = 1.5.

questions.q_text: The pressure of a gas is 1.6 x 10^5 Pa and its density is 3 kg/m^3. The rms speed of its molecules is
questions.solution: P = (1/3) rho v_rms^2, so v_rms = sqrt(3P/rho) = sqrt(3 x 1.6e5/3) = 400 m/s.

questions.q_text: At the same temperature, the ratio of the rms speeds of hydrogen (M = 2) and oxygen (M = 32) molecules is
questions.solution: v_rms is proportional to 1/sqrt(M), so the ratio is sqrt(32/2) = 4 : 1.

questions.q_text: At what temperature will the rms speed of oxygen molecules (M = 32) equal the rms speed of hydrogen molecules (M = 2) at 300 K?
questions.solution: Equate 3RT/32 = 3R(300)/2, giving T = 300 x 16 = 4800 K.

questions.q_text: A particle executes SHM described by y = 5 sin(4 pi t) cm, where t is in seconds. Its time period is
questions.solution: omega = 4 pi rad/s, so T = 2 pi/omega = 2 pi/(4 pi) = 0.5 s.

questions.q_text: A particle in SHM has amplitude 5 cm and angular frequency 20 rad/s. Its maximum speed is
questions.solution: v_max = A omega = 0.05 x 20 = 1 m/s.

questions.q_text: A particle executes SHM of amplitude 5 cm and period 2 s. Its speed when it is 3 cm from the mean position is
questions.solution: v = omega sqrt(A^2 - x^2) = pi x sqrt(25 - 9) = 4 pi cm/s.

questions.q_text: A block of mass 1 kg attached to a spring of force constant 100 N/m oscillates on a smooth horizontal surface. Its time period is nearly
questions.solution: T = 2 pi sqrt(m/k) = 2 pi sqrt(1/100) = 0.628 s.

questions.q_text: A mass suspended from a spring of force constant k has period T. If two such identical springs are joined end to end and the same mass is suspended, the new period is
questions.solution: Springs in series give k_eff = k/2, and T is proportional to 1/sqrt(k), so the period becomes sqrt(2) T.

questions.q_text: The length of a seconds pendulum (time period 2 s) at a place where g = 10 m/s^2 is nearly
In simple harmonic motion, the phase difference between the displacement and the acceleration of the particle is
questions.solution: a = -omega^2 y, so acceleration is always opposite to displacement, a phase difference of pi rad.

questions.q_text: For a particle in SHM of amplitude A, the ratio of its kinetic energy to its potential energy at displacement A/2 from the mean position is
questions.solution: KE proportional to (A^2 - x^2) = 3A^2/4 and PE proportional to x^2 = A^2/4, so KE : PE = 3 : 1.

questions.q_text: A body of mass 0.2 kg executes SHM of amplitude 0.1 m and angular frequency 10 rad/s. Its total mechanical energy is
Two SHMs along the same line are represented by y1 = 3 sin(omega t) and y2 = 4 cos(omega t) in cm. The amplitude of the resultant motion is
questions.solution: The two differ in phase by pi/2, so the resultant amplitude = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5 cm.

questions.q_text: A spring of force constant k is cut into two equal halves and one half is used with the same mass, which earlier gave period T. The new period of oscillation is
questions.solution: Halving the length doubles the force constant to 2k, so T' = T/sqrt(2).

questions.q_text: A simple pendulum of period T on the ground is taken into a lift moving downward with acceleration g/2. Its new period becomes
questions.solution: Effective gravity g_eff = g - g/2 = g/2, and T is proportional to 1/sqrt(g_eff), so T' = sqrt(2) T.

questions.q_text: A progressive wave is represented by y = 0.05 sin(100 pi t - 0.5 pi x), where all quantities are in SI units. The speed of the wave is
questions.solution: v = omega/k = 100 pi/(0.5 pi) = 200 m/s.

questions.q_text: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. The number of beats heard per second is
questions.solution: Beat frequency = difference of the frequencies = 260 - 256 = 4 per second.

questions.q_text: The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe of length 0.5 m is (speed of sound in air = 340 m/s)
questions.solution: For a pipe closed at one end, f = v/(4L) = 340/(4 x 0.5) = 170 Hz.

questions.q_text: A pipe closed at one end and open at the other supports standing waves whose frequencies are
questions.opt_a: Only multiples of three of the fundamental
questions.opt_b: All integral multiples of the fundamental
questions.opt_c: Only even multiples of the fundamental
questions.opt_d: Only odd multiples of the fundamental
questions.solution: A closed pipe has a node at the closed end and antinode at the open end, so only odd harmonics (1, 3, 5, ...) are present.

questions.q_text: A stretched string of length 1 m and linear mass density 0.01 kg/m is under a tension of 100 N. Its fundamental frequency of vibration is
The speed of a transverse wave on a string of linear mass density 0.04 kg/m under a tension of 64 N is
questions.solution: v = sqrt(T/mu) = sqrt(64/0.04) = sqrt(1600) = 40 m/s.

questions.q_text: A source emitting sound of frequency 300 Hz moves towards a stationary observer with a speed of 40 m/s. The frequency heard by the observer is (speed of sound = 340 m/s)
An observer moves towards a stationary source of sound of frequency 500 Hz with a speed of 34 m/s. The apparent frequency heard is (speed of sound = 340 m/s)
A source of sound of frequency 550 Hz recedes from a stationary observer with a speed of 34 m/s. The frequency heard by the observer is (speed of sound = 340 m/s)

A tuning fork gives 4 beats per second with a standard fork of frequency 256 Hz. On loading the first fork with a little wax the beat frequency rises to 6 per second. The original frequency of the first fork was
questions.solution: Wax lowers the frequency of the loaded fork; the beats increase only if it was 252 Hz (256 - 4).

questions.q_text: A stationary wave is described by y = 2 sin(0.1 pi x) cos(100 pi t), with x in metres. The distance between two consecutive nodes is
questions.solution: k = 0.1 pi so the wavelength is 20 m; consecutive nodes are lambda/2 = 10 m apart.

questions.q_text: Two waves of the same frequency and equal amplitude a travelling in the same direction have a constant phase difference of 60 degrees. The amplitude of the resultant wave is
questions.solution: A = 2a cos(phi/2) = 2a cos(30 degrees) = sqrt(3) a.

questions.q_text: The third harmonic of a pipe closed at one end has the same frequency as the first overtone of an open pipe. The ratio of the length of the closed pipe to that of the open pipe is
questions.solution: 3v/(4 Lc) = 2v/(2 Lo) gives 3 Lo = 4 Lc, so Lc : Lo = 3 : 4.

questions.q_text: Two point charges of 2 microC and 3 microC are placed 30 cm apart in vacuum. The magnitude of the electrostatic force between them is
An infinite plane sheet carries a uniform surface charge density of 8.85 x 10^-6 C/m^2. The electric field just outside the sheet is
questions.solution: For an infinite sheet E = sigma/(2 epsilon0) = 8.85 x 10^-6 / (2 x 8.85 x 10^-12) = 5 x 10^5 N/C.

questions.q_text: A point charge q lies at the centre of a spherical Gaussian surface of radius r. If the radius of the surface is doubled, keeping the charge unchanged, the electric flux through it
questions.opt_a: becomes half of its earlier value
questions.opt_b: becomes one fourth of its earlier value
questions.solution: By Gauss law flux = q_enclosed/epsilon0, which depends only on the enclosed charge and not on the size of the surface.

questions.q_text: An infinitely long straight wire carries a uniform linear charge density of 2 x 10^-6 C/m. The electric field at a point 10 cm from the wire is
Charges +5 nC and -5 nC are separated by 4 mm forming a short dipole. The electric field at a point 20 cm from the centre of the dipole on its axial line is
Three capacitors of 2 microF, 3 microF and 6 microF are joined in series. The equivalent capacitance of the combination is
A 10 microF capacitor is charged to a potential difference of 200 V. The energy stored in it is

A parallel plate capacitor is charged to 100 V and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric slab of dielectric constant 5 is now inserted so as to fill the space between the plates. The new potential difference across the capacitor is
questions.solution: With the battery removed the charge is constant, so V = Q/C and C becomes KC; V_new = 100/5 = 20 V.

questions.q_text: A parallel plate air capacitor has plates of area 100 cm^2 separated by 1 mm. Its capacitance is (epsilon0 = 8.85 x 10^-12 SI units)
The electric potential at a point 30 cm from the centre of a short electric dipole of dipole moment 2 x 10^-9 C m, on its axial line, is
A 2 microF capacitor charged to 100 V is connected across an uncharged 3 microF capacitor. The energy dissipated in the process is
A copper wire of cross sectional area 1 mm^2 carries a current of 1.6 A. If the free electron density is 8 x 10^28 per m^3, the drift speed of the electrons is
A wire of resistance 5 ohm is stretched uniformly so that its length becomes twice the original length. Its new resistance is
questions.solution: On stretching at constant volume R is proportional to l^2, so R_new = 5 x 2^2 = 20 ohm.

questions.q_text: Applying Kirchhoff loop rule to a single loop, a cell of emf 12 V sends a current of 2 A through an external resistance of 5 ohm. The internal resistance of the cell is
questions.solution: E = I(R + r) gives 12 = 2(5 + r), so r = 1 ohm.

questions.q_text: Resistances of 4 ohm, 6 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is
In a metre bridge the balance point is obtained at 40 cm from the left end when a known resistance of 6 ohm is in the left gap. The unknown resistance in the right gap is
questions.solution: R/X = l/(100 - l) gives X = 6 x 60/40 = 9 ohm.

questions.q_text: A potentiometer wire of length 4 m has a potential difference of 6 V across it. A cell connected to the wire is balanced at a length of 1.2 m. The emf of the cell is
questions.solution: Potential gradient = 6/4 = 1.5 V/m; emf = 1.5 x 1.2 = 1.8 V.

questions.q_text: A uniform wire of total resistance 12 ohm is bent to form a closed circle. The resistance between two diametrically opposite points of the circle is
questions.solution: The two halves of 6 ohm each are in parallel: R = (6 x 6)/(6 + 6) = 3 ohm.

questions.q_text: A circular coil of 100 turns and radius 10 cm carries a current of 1 A. The magnetic field at its centre is
A solenoid of length 50 cm has 1000 turns and carries a current of 5 A. The magnetic field near its middle on the axis is
Two long parallel wires 10 cm apart carry currents of 10 A each in the same direction. The force per unit length between them is
questions.solution: F/L = mu0 I1 I2/(2 pi d) = 2 x 10^-7 x 100/0.1 = 2 x 10^-4 N/m; parallel currents in the same direction attract.

questions.q_text: An electron moving with a speed of 2 x 10^6 m/s enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.1 T at right angles to it. The radius of its circular path is
A square coil of side 10 cm having 50 turns carries a current of 2 A. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T with its plane parallel to the field. The torque acting on the coil is
questions.solution: tau = NIAB sin theta; with the plane parallel to B, theta = 90 degrees, so tau = 50 x 2 x 0.01 x 0.5 = 0.5 N m.

questions.q_text: A galvanometer of resistance 50 ohm gives a full scale deflection for a current of 2 mA. To convert it into a voltmeter of range 10 V, one must connect
questions.solution: R = V/Ig - G = 10/0.002 - 50 = 4950 ohm, connected in series with the galvanometer.

questions.q_text: A short bar magnet of magnetic moment 4 A m^2 produces a magnetic field at a point 20 cm from its centre on its axis equal to
A bar magnet of magnetic moment 2 A m^2 is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.1 T making an angle of 30 degrees with the field. The torque on the magnet is
questions.solution: tau = MB sin theta = 2 x 0.1 x sin 30 = 0.1 N m.

questions.q_text: At a certain place the horizontal component of the earth magnetic field is 0.3 G and the angle of dip is 60 degrees. The total intensity of the earth magnetic field there is
questions.solution: Bh = B cos(dip), so B = 0.3/cos 60 = 0.6 G.

questions.q_text: A substance placed in a non uniform magnetic field moves from the stronger to the weaker part of the field and has a small negative susceptibility. The substance is
questions.solution: Diamagnetic materials have small negative susceptibility and are feebly repelled by a magnetic field.

questions.q_text: A bar magnet oscillating in a uniform magnetic field has a time period T. The magnet is cut into two equal pieces by a cut perpendicular to its length and one piece is made to oscillate in the same field. The new time period is
questions.solution: For each half M is halved and the moment of inertia becomes I/8, so T is proportional to sqrt(I/M) giving T_new = T/2.

questions.q_text: The magnetic flux linked with a coil of one turn changes from 0.05 Wb to 0.01 Wb in 0.02 s. The average induced emf is
questions.solution: emf = -dphi/dt = (0.05 - 0.01)/0.02 = 2 V in magnitude.

questions.q_text: A conducting rod of length 0.5 m moves with a velocity of 10 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. The emf induced across its ends is
questions.solution: Motional emf = Blv = 0.2 x 0.5 x 10 = 1 V.

questions.q_text: The energy stored in an inductor of self inductance 2 H carrying a steady current of 3 A is
The current in a primary coil changes uniformly from 0 to 10 A in 0.5 s and induces an emf of 20 V in a neighbouring secondary coil. The mutual inductance of the pair is
questions.solution: emf = M dI/dt gives M = 20 x 0.5/10 = 1 H.

questions.q_text: The north pole of a bar magnet is moved towards a closed circular coil. According to Lenz law, the induced current in the coil is such that
questions.opt_a: the face of the coil towards the magnet becomes a north pole and opposes the approach
questions.opt_b: the face of the coil towards the magnet becomes a south pole and attracts the magnet
questions.opt_c: no current flows because the magnet is not in contact with the coil
questions.opt_d: the induced current is independent of the direction of motion of the magnet
questions.solution: The induced effects oppose the change producing them, so the near face becomes a north pole and repels the approaching north pole.

questions.q_text: A solenoid of length 50 cm with 1000 turns has a cross sectional area of 10 cm^2. Its self inductance is
An alternating voltage is given by V = 200 sin(314 t) volt. The frequency of the source is nearly
questions.solution: omega = 314 rad/s, so f = omega/2pi = 314/6.28 = 50 Hz.

questions.q_text: A series circuit contains an inductor of 0.5 H and a capacitor of 8 microF. The angular frequency at which the circuit resonates is
questions.solution: omega = 1/sqrt(LC) = 1/sqrt(0.5 x 8 x 10^-6) = 500 rad/s.

questions.q_text: In a series LCR circuit R = 30 ohm, XL = 60 ohm and XC = 20 ohm. The impedance of the circuit is
An ideal transformer steps down 220 V to 22 V. If the primary has 1000 turns, the number of turns in the secondary is
questions.solution: Ns/Np = Vs/Vp gives Ns = 1000 x 22/220 = 100 turns.

questions.q_text: A series LCR circuit with R = 30 ohm, XL = 60 ohm and XC = 20 ohm is connected to a 200 V rms source. The average power consumed is
questions.solution: Z = 50 ohm, I = 200/50 = 4 A, P = I^2 R = 16 x 30 = 480 W (power factor 0.6).

questions.q_text: Which of the following arrangements of electromagnetic radiations is in the order of increasing frequency?
questions.opt_a: gamma rays, X rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwaves, radio waves
questions.opt_b: microwaves, radio waves, infrared, ultraviolet, visible, X rays, gamma rays
questions.opt_c: infrared, visible, radio waves, microwaves, ultraviolet, gamma rays, X rays
questions.opt_d: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X rays, gamma rays
questions.solution: Frequency increases as wavelength decreases, giving radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X ray and gamma ray.

questions.q_text: In a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum the peak value of the magnetic field is 20 nT. The peak value of the electric field is
A radio station broadcasts at a frequency of 100 MHz. The wavelength of the radio waves emitted is
An electromagnetic wave carrying 6 J of energy is completely absorbed by a surface. The momentum delivered to the surface is
questions.solution: For total absorption p = U/c = 6/(3 x 10^8) = 2 x 10^-8 kg m/s.

questions.q_text: During the charging of a parallel plate capacitor, the displacement current between the plates
questions.opt_a: is equal to the conduction current in the connecting wires
questions.opt_b: is zero because no charge flows between the plates
questions.opt_c: is always greater than the conduction current
questions.opt_d: exists only if a dielectric is present between the plates
questions.solution: Displacement current id = epsilon0 dphiE/dt and it exactly equals the conduction current, keeping Ampere Maxwell law consistent.

questions.q_text: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image is formed at
questions.opt_a: 60 cm behind the mirror and is virtual
questions.opt_b: 12 cm in front of the mirror and is real
questions.opt_c: 15 cm behind the mirror and is virtual
questions.opt_d: 60 cm in front of the mirror and is real
questions.solution: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f with u = -30 cm and f = -20 cm gives v = -60 cm, a real image 60 cm in front.

questions.q_text: An object is placed 15 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The magnification produced is
questions.solution: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f gives v = 30 cm, so m = v/u = 30/(-15) = -2, a real inverted image twice the size.

questions.q_text: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. The focal length of the combination is
questions.solution: 1/F = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60, so F = +60 cm and the combination behaves as a converging lens.

questions.q_text: The refractive index of a medium with respect to air is 2. The critical angle for total internal reflection at the medium air interface is
questions.solution: sin C = 1/n = 0.5, so C = 30 degrees.

questions.q_text: The angle of a prism is 60 degrees and the angle of minimum deviation for it is 30 degrees. The refractive index of the material of the prism is
questions.solution: n = sin[(A + Dm)/2]/sin(A/2) = sin 45/sin 30 = 1.41.

questions.q_text: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment has an objective of focal length 100 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 5 cm. Its magnifying power and tube length are
questions.solution: M = fo/fe = 100/5 = 20 and L = fo + fe = 105 cm.

questions.q_text: A thin converging lens of glass of refractive index 1.5 has a focal length of 10 cm in air. When it is completely immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.6, its focal length becomes
questions.solution: 1/f is proportional to (n_lens/n_medium - 1), so f_liquid = 10 x 0.5/(1.5/1.6 - 1) = -80 cm, the lens now diverges.

questions.q_text: In Young double slit experiment light of wavelength 600 nm is used with slits 1 mm apart and a screen 1 m away. The fringe width is
The whole Young double slit apparatus that gives a fringe width of 0.6 mm in air is immersed in water of refractive index 4/3. The new fringe width is
questions.solution: In a medium lambda becomes lambda/n, so beta_new = 0.6/(4/3) = 0.45 mm.

questions.q_text: Light of wavelength 600 nm falls normally on a single slit of width 0.3 mm and the diffraction pattern is observed on a screen 1.5 m away. The width of the central maximum is
The refractive index of a transparent medium is 1.732. The angle of incidence at which light reflected from its surface is completely plane polarised is
questions.solution: By Brewster law tan ip = n = 1.732, so ip = 60 degrees.

questions.q_text: In an interference experiment the widths of the two slits are in the ratio 4 : 1. The ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in the fringe pattern is
questions.solution: Intensity is proportional to slit width so I1/I2 = 4 and a1/a2 = 2; Imax/Imin = [(2+1)/(2-1)]^2 = 9.

questions.q_text: The energy of a photon of light of wavelength 6630 A is
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q_text: The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission from a metal surface is 4140 A. The work function of the metal is nearly
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q_text: Light of photon energy 4 eV falls on a metal whose work function is 2.5 eV. The stopping potential for the emitted photoelectrons is
questions.solution: eV0 = E - W = 4 - 2.5 = 1.5 eV, so the stopping potential is 1.5 V.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q_text: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 V. Its de Broglie wavelength is nearly
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q_text: A body of mass 100 g moves with a speed of 66.3 m/s. Its de Broglie wavelength is
questions.solution: lambda = h/mv = 6.63 x 10^-34/(0.1 x 66.3) = 1 x 10^-34 m, far too small to be detected.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q_text: In the photoelectric effect, if the intensity of the incident light is doubled while its frequency is kept unchanged, then
questions.opt_a: the photoelectric current doubles but the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons is unchanged
questions.opt_b: both the current and the maximum kinetic energy double
questions.opt_c: the maximum kinetic energy doubles but the current is unchanged
questions.opt_d: neither the current nor the maximum kinetic energy changes
questions.solution: Intensity fixes the number of photons and hence the current, while the maximum kinetic energy hv - W depends only on frequency.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q_text: The radius of the third orbit of the hydrogen atom in Bohr model is (radius of the first orbit is 0.53 A)
The energy of the electron in the second orbit of the hydrogen atom is
The energy required to remove the electron from the ground state of a singly ionised helium atom is
questions.solution: E_n = -13.6 Z^2/n^2 eV; for He+ with Z = 2 and n = 1, E = -54.4 eV, so 54.4 eV is needed.

questions.q_text: The energy of the photon emitted when a hydrogen atom makes a transition from n = 3 to n = 2 is
Which spectral series of the hydrogen atom lies wholly in the visible region of the spectrum?
questions.solution: Transitions ending at n = 2 form the Balmer series, whose prominent lines lie in the visible region.

questions.q_text: The angular momentum of the electron in the second Bohr orbit of the hydrogen atom is
The ratio of the radii of two nuclei having mass numbers 27 and 64 is
questions.solution: R is proportional to A^(1/3), so the ratio is 27^(1/3) : 64^(1/3) = 3 : 4.

questions.q_text: The mass defect of a certain nucleus is 0.2 u. Its binding energy is
questions.solution: BE = (mass defect) x 931.5 MeV = 0.2 x 931.5 = 186.3 MeV.

questions.q_text: A radioactive sample of mass 16 g has a half life of 5 days. The mass of the sample left undecayed after 20 days is
questions.solution: 20 days is 4 half lives, so mass left = 16 x (1/2)^4 = 1 g.

questions.q_text: The half life of a radioactive nuclide is 138.6 days. Its decay constant is
A nucleus of mass number A and atomic number Z emits one alpha particle followed by two beta minus particles. The final nucleus has
questions.opt_a: mass number A - 4 and atomic number Z - 2
questions.opt_b: mass number A - 4 and atomic number Z + 2
questions.opt_c: mass number A - 4 and atomic number Z, an isotope of the original nucleus
questions.opt_d: mass number A and atomic number Z - 2
questions.solution: Alpha emission gives (A-4, Z-2) and each beta minus raises Z by one, so the product is (A-4, Z), an isotope of the parent.

questions.q_text: In the fusion reaction of deuterium (2.0141 u) and tritium (3.0160 u) producing helium (4.0026 u) and a neutron (1.0087 u), the energy released is nearly
In a p type semiconductor obtained by doping germanium with indium, the majority charge carriers are
questions.solution: A trivalent dopant creates vacant bonds, so holes are the majority carriers in a p type semiconductor.

questions.q_text: If the two inputs of a NAND gate are joined together, the resulting gate behaves as
questions.solution: With both inputs equal to A the output is NOT(A AND A) = NOT A, so it acts as an inverter.

questions.q_text: A full wave rectifier is fed with an ac supply of frequency 50 Hz. The fundamental ripple frequency of the output is
questions.solution: A full wave rectifier gives one output pulse per half cycle, so the ripple frequency is twice the input frequency.

questions.q_text: A silicon diode with a forward voltage drop of 0.7 V is connected in series with a 500 ohm resistor across a 5 V battery in forward bias. The current in the circuit is
In a common emitter amplifier the current gain beta is 50 and the collector load is 5 kilo ohm. If the base current changes by 20 microA, the change in output voltage is
questions.solution: Change in collector current = 50 x 20 microA = 1 mA; output voltage change = 1 mA x 5 kilo ohm = 5 V.
